title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1LC0RD_1LA0LD_1LE0RA_0LB---_0LB1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1LC0RD_1LA0LD_1LE0RA_0LB---_0LB1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The left side is a pile of segments xk (x = 10111110) that the head sweeps over; Lean proves the three shift rules of a sweep. The rule that moves the separators between segments, and the counter at the right end, are not decoded. No halt in 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 33,783 cells have been visited and 18,178 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.482). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0).

claims.title: The shift rules of a sweep
claims.text: Going right, F turns each word x = 10111110 into y = 10011001 (26 steps a word, right_pass); going left, B turns them back (20 steps a word, left_pass); at the left end A starts the next pass over the leading segment (left_end). For every n and every tape around.

claims.title: The pile of segments
claims.text: At step 2,266,312,097 the left side is 112 segments xk with lengths falling from 218 to 1 towards the start, separated mostly by 1010 or (10)^4 and by a few longer markers (1 0 1^9 0, 1 0 1^13 0). Each sweep adds one x to the leading segment (about 148,000 steps a sweep at that width); when it reaches about 218 a new segment starts.

claims.title: No small closed tape language
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with windows K = 3, 4, 5 leaves a halt (E reading 1) reachable in the abstraction.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.10×10<sup>10</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.10×1010 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.00×1010 steps. No trip-level jump was used in this run, only the shift rules over repeated words (exact by induction, but the program is not verified).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: the rule that moves the separators and the right-end counter are not decoded, so the question is not yet reduced to a map.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LE_0RC---_1RD0LA_1RE0RA_1LC0LF_0RC1LC up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine sweeps back and forth over a growing pile of segments made of one 8-cell word, while a small counter ticks at the right end. The sweeps are understood; what the separators between the segments do is not, yet.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
The shift rules of a sweep, proved for every length.
Segments of the word 10111110 at 2.3·10<sup>9</sup> steps.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.00×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.482). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0).
After 109 steps the tape spans 33,783 cells (24,855 left of the start, 33 right), with a density of 1s of 0.538.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A pile of segments of one word
html: Almost all of the tape is left of the start, and it is made of the word x = 10111110. At step 2,266,312,097, read from the far left, it is 1^2 0 1^3 0 x 1^13 0 x^218 1^5 0 x^206 (10)^2 x^205 (10)^2 x^209 …: 112 segments xk whose lengths fall from about 218 at the left to 1 near the start, separated by short markers, mostly 1010 or (10)^4. The few cells right of the start form a separate, slowly growing structure (35 cells after 7.8·108 steps).

sections.heading: Rewrite going right, rewrite back going left
html: The head runs right over the pile in state F turning every x into y = 10011001 (26 steps a word), then left in state B turning every y back into x (20 steps a word). At the far left the configuration A>0 1 x^k becomes A>0 1 x^(k+1) one sweep later: the leading segment gains one word per sweep. These shift rules are proved in Lean for every length.

What is not decoded is what happens at the separators: the markers change from sweep to sweep (a (10)^4 becomes 1 0 1^9 0, then 1 0 1^13 0, …), which looks like digits being carried across the pile, and the far-left segment is cut off when it reaches about 218 words.

sections.heading: Not yet reduced
html: The only halting transition is E reading 1. A small closed language (windows of 3–5 cells) still allows it, and the macro rule of the separators is not known, so the halting question has not been turned into a statement about a map. This machine is left with notes for later.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LE_0RC---_1RD0LA_1RE0RA_1LC0LF_0RC1LC: rename A→E, B→C, C→D, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror

summary: A bouncer over a growing pile of segments of the word 10111110 (the head rewrites them to 10011001 going right and back going left), with a slowly growing counter at the right end; its macro rule is not found yet.
